purpose: First-party facts from the maker's own documents, compared against data/specs/singer-hd6700c.json. Research input for the editor; not a spec file.

documents.note: US singer.com page. Lists 411 stitch applications, 1 lettering font, 7 buttonhole styles, 6.4 in needle to tower, 1100/min, warranty 25/1, 0.7 A. Price shown as $419.99 MSRP with a sale price; no weight.

One manual titled 'HD 6700C - HD 6705C'. It covers two models and does not say which features differ, so every row from it is shared-manual evidence. The linked widen URL with ?t.download=true returns an HTML viewer; the /content/.../pdf/ path returns the real PDF.

documents.type: warranty PDF (SVP Worldwide Limited Warranty 25/1, English, French, Spanish)
documents.note: The PDF linked from the 6700C product page. Generic text: product frame 25 years, parts and adjustments 1 year. Does not name models.
Groups models by warranty. Lists 6380, 6600C and 6800C under Limited 25/1; the 6700C is not named on the page. 4452, 4432 and 3342 sit under 25/2/90.
Singer's Heavy Duty picks page: 6600C, 6700C and 6800C side by side with built-in stitch counts.
6800C page, shown out of stock on fetch date (page wording: Out of Stock, Sold out).
6620C page, shown out of stock on fetch date (page wording: Out of Stock, Sold out).
Returned HTTP 404 Not Found on fetch date. The 6600C extension-table bundle page was still listed on the Singer homepage.

facts.value: 1100 stitches per minute on the product page ('High Speed Stitching (1100/min)'); manual technical specification says Maximum 1000 +/- 50 rpm (straight stitch, default length)
facts.note: Page and manual disagree. The manual is the technical spec but covers both the 6700C and 6705C. Our 1100 matches the product page only. The Singer comparison page does not give the 6700C speed (it gives 1,050 for the 6800C).

site.label: Speed
site.juki: Product page: 1100/min. Manual (shared 6700C and 6705C): maximum 1000 +/- 50 rpm.

facts.value: 200 built-in stitches, 411 stitch applications, per the Singer Good/Better/Best page; the product page gives only '411 Stitch Applications' and the manual gives no plain count in its text
facts.note: The spec has stitchCount null. Singer's own comparison page states 200 built-in stitches and 411 applications. The product page says 411 applications and defines an application as a technique, not a stitch. The same product page prose also says 'Among the 586 stitch applications', a figure that appears to be copied from the 6800C page. Two Singer pages, one number each for the stitch count; the manual's stitch charts are images and were not counted.

site.label: Stitches
site.juki: Comparison page: 200 built-in stitches, 411 applications. Product page: 411 applications (prose also says 586).
site.others: Dealers and Amazon say 411 stitch applications.

facts.value: 1 lettering font on the product page highlights; 2 lettering fonts on the Singer comparison page; manual shows a Block Font under Stitch Menu 4, 7 mm letter height
facts.note: Singer's own pages disagree on the font count (1 vs 2). Dealer 'one comparison site counts 2' in our spec note matches the comparison page.

site.label: Lettering
site.juki: Product page: 1 lettering font. Comparison page: 2 lettering fonts. Letters 7 mm.

facts.value: 6.4 in (163 mm), described as needle to tower; page also gives sewing space height 4.6 in
facts.note: Maker wording is 'sewing space (needle to tower)' and 'distance from needle to the tower'. The Singer comparison page gives 8.3 in of throat for the 6800C, which conflicts with the 6800C product page (6.4 in); this is a 6800C issue, noted so the sibling comparison is not read off the wrong page.

facts.value: 7 one-step buttonhole styles (page); manual describes a one-step buttonhole sewn to the button size

Page: 'Warranty (25/1)', 'Up to 25 Year Warranty Coverage', linked PDF is the generic 25/1 text: frame 25 years free replacement parts at buyer's labor cost; parts and adjustments 1 year. Not model-specific text. The maker warranty page lists 6600C and 6800C under 25/1 and does not name the 6700C.
facts.spec_value: 25 yr limited on machine head, 2 yr on motor, light, wiring, switches, speed control and electronics, 90 days on adjustments, belts, rings, bulbs and attachments
facts.note: Our 25/2/90 matches the maker's 25/2/90 tier (4452, 4432, 3342), which does not list the 6700C. The 6700C product page says 25/1 and links the 25/1 PDF. The Amazon listing shows '1 Year Manufacturer'. Recommend the editor changes the spec to 25/1 with the product page and PDF as sources. Warranty is for original purchaser from Singer or an authorized dealer; household use only; the PDF names no model.

site.label: Warranty
site.juki: Product page: 25/1. PDF: 25-year frame, 1-year parts and adjustments. Limited, original purchaser, authorized sellers.
site.others: Our earlier figure was 25/2/90 (a different Singer tier).

facts.value: 'powerful motor' and 'extra high sewing speed'; electrical rating 0.7 A, 120 V, 60 Hz; no wattage published; no motor type on the 6700C page
facts.spec_value: Singer describes a powerful motor with extra high sewing speed; wattage not published
facts.note: The 6800C page adds '60% stronger than a standard sewing machine motor'; the 6700C page does not carry that sentence.

site.label: Motor
site.juki: Powerful motor, 0.7 A, 120 V. No wattage.
site.others: Walmart title: 'Strong Motor with Enhanced Piercing Power'.

facts.value: 7 kg (about 15.4 lb) in the shared manual's technical specification; machine size about 440 x 190 x 280 mm; the product page gives 17.3 x 7.5 x 10.9 in and no weight
facts.note: 7 kg converts to 15.4 lb, which matches our figure. The Amazon 14.6 lb and blog 16.3 lb remain outliers. Manual is shared with the 6705C. Dimensions: product page 17.3 x 7.5 x 10.9 in; Amazon 17.5 x 7.5 x 11 in.

site.label: Weight
site.juki: Manual: 7 kg (about 15.4 lb). Product page lists no weight.

facts.value: Manual: a Needle Up/Down button and a Needle Up/Down setting (default needle up) are documented; the 6700C product page does not list Needle Up/Down as a feature; the 6800C and 6620C product pages do
facts.spec_value: None; no needle up/down button (handwheel positions the needle), per bobbinhub
facts.note: Our spec says no needle up/down, sourced to a comparison blog. The manual documents a needle up/down button, but it is the shared 6700C and 6705C manual and does not say which model has it. The product page for the 6700C omits it while the 6800C and 6620C pages list it. Leave unverified; the editor must decide.

site.label: Needle up/down
site.juki: Shared manual documents the button; the 6700C product page does not list it.

facts.value: Manual: Start/Stop button runs the machine without the foot control; manual also lists a Reverse button that sews three tie-off stitches on many stitches; product page lists a Tie-Off button
facts.note: Shared 6700C and 6705C manual. The product page does not list a start/stop button. Treat as unverified for the 6700C alone.

site.label: Start/stop
site.juki: Shared manual documents a Start/Stop button.
site.others: The blog we cited lists start/stop as a 6800C feature.

facts.value: Product page lists a Tie-Off button and no thread cutter button. The manual's machine overview lists a 'Thread Knife' for trimming thread ends (a side cutter, not an automatic cutter). The 6800C page lists a 'Thread Cutter Button trims top & bottom threads'.
facts.spec_value: None; a tie-off button is included and the automatic thread cutter is listed as a 6800C feature
facts.note: Do not read 'Thread Knife' in the manual as an automatic trimmer.

site.label: Thread trimmer
site.juki: No thread cutter listed; Tie-Off Button. (Manual: hand thread knife.)

facts.value: Speed Control lever: sets the maximum sewing speed; manual: cannot exceed the stitch's default maximum
facts.spec_value: Speed control slider; no needle up/down button (handwheel positions the needle)

facts.value: Heavy Duty Metal Frame: 'the machine's interior frame is metal'; stainless steel bed plate
facts.spec_value: Full metal interior frame, stainless steel bedplate

site.label: Frame
site.juki: Interior frame is metal; stainless steel bed plate

facts.value: Presser foot rise height 6 mm (manual technical specification)
facts.note: Shared manual. Stitch width 0 to 7.0 mm; stitch length 0 to 4.5 mm; LED lamp; four stitch menus (utility, utility and decorative, decorative, alphabet).

facts.value: Product page list: all-purpose, zipper, buttonhole, blind hem, button sewing, Sew Easy, satin stitch, even feed (walking), open toe, cording feet; 4 Class 15 bobbins, large and small spool holders, spool pin felt, auxiliary spool pin, L-screwdriver, brush and seam ripper, soft cover, pack of needles; '$185 included accessories'
facts.spec_value: 10 presser feet incl. walking foot, 4 bobbins, soft cover

site.label: Feet
site.juki: 10 feet incl. even feed (walking) foot, 4 bobbins, soft cover

facts.value: MSRP $419.99 (singer.com original price) with a sale price of $329.99 on the page; extension table bundle on singer.com $349.99 against $488.98 original
facts.note: Page-seen sale price, not a maker list price statement beyond the struck 'Original price'/MSRP. Not for chrome.

facts.value: Marketing wording: 'workhorse with endless possibilities'; 'designed with your heavy duty projects in mind, from denim to canvas'; 'powerful motor ... extra high sewing speed'; 'Professional speed for faster results' (1100/min); 'Having a generous "C" space allows you to sew larger projects like quilts with ease'; 'Heavy Duty' is the series name
facts.note: All maker claims, to be quoted as claims. No duty rating, no sewing-layer or fabric-thickness spec is published.

site.label: Claims
site.juki: Heavy Duty name; denim to canvas; quilts with ease; professional speed

facts.value: Singer 6700C product page shows the machine for sale; the 6600C product page returned 404; the 6800C and 6620C pages showed Out of Stock
facts.note: Page wording on 2026-10-02 only. Singer's homepage announces a 2026 'next evolution' Heavy Duty line (4511, 4523, 4532, 4552 with a new DC motor); it does not name the 6700C.
